Session 6 · Automate with AI

Set up n8n and run your first AI workflow

A step-by-step walkthrough: from creating an account to a workflow that reads job applications and scores them.

Press → to begin

The route: 34 steps in 7 parts

  2. 2Welcome surveysteps 6–10
  3. 3Your workspacesteps 11–16

Part 1 · Create your accountStep 1 of 34

Open n8n.io

Go to n8n.io. The homepage shows what we are building toward: an agent whose workflow you can open and follow, step by step. Click GET STARTED (top right).

Part 1 · Create your accountStep 2 of 34

Enter your email

On the Create account page, type the email for your trial and click Continue. It is a free 14-day trial and no credit card is required.

Part 1 · Create your accountStep 3 of 34

Verify your email

n8n emails you a 6-digit code. Click VERIFY MY EMAIL in the message, or return to the sign-up page and type the code.

Part 1 · Create your accountStep 4 of 34

Finish creating your account

Add your full name and a password (8+ characters, at least one number and one uppercase letter). Then choose an instance name.

Part 1 · Create your accountStep 5 of 34

Name your instance

The instance name becomes your personal URL: name.app.n8n.cloud (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). Pass the Cloudflare check, then click Start free 14-day trial.

Part 2 · Welcome surveyStep 6 of 34

Survey 1 of 5: company size

n8n asks a few quick questions to tailor your trial. First: the size of your company. Pick any option and click OK.

Part 2 · Welcome surveyStep 7 of 34

Survey 2 of 5: your role

What best describes your role? Choose one and click OK.

Part 2 · Welcome surveyStep 8 of 34

Survey 3 of 5: how you heard about n8n

Pick the option that fits and click OK.

Part 2 · Welcome surveyStep 9 of 34

Survey 4 of 5: what to automate

Do you already know what you want to automate? Choose Not yet or Yes and click OK.

Part 2 · Welcome surveyStep 10 of 34

Survey 5 of 5: comfort without AI

Select as many items as you like (or None of the above), then click Submit.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 11 of 34

Your instance is ready

n8n launches your cloud instance in under a minute. While you wait, the AI Assistant preview shows a workflow built from one plain-English sentence. Click Start automating.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 12 of 34

Meet the n8n Assistant

You land on the Assistant: “What do you want to automate?” Dismiss the “Talk to your agents here” tip with Got it.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 13 of 34

Signing back in

Coming back later? n8n emails you a magic sign-in link. Click it and you arrive here with no password to type.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 14 of 34

Tour the sidebar

Left sidebar: New chat, Overview and Personal (your projects). At the bottom: Cloud console, Templates, Insights, Help and Settings.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 15 of 34

Create a new workflow

Click the + button at the top of the sidebar. The menu offers New workflow, agent, credential, folder, variable, data table, project and AI chat. Choose New workflow.

Part 3 · Your workspaceStep 16 of 34

Open the workflow menu

A blank canvas opens with Add first step… or Build with AI. Click the ⋯ menu next to “My workflow” to see Rename, Duplicate, Share, Export JSON and Import.

Part 4 · Import the ready-made workflowStep 17 of 34

Import → From file

Hover Import, then choose From file. This loads a workflow someone else already built, saved as a .json file.

Part 4 · Import the ready-made workflowStep 18 of 34

Find the workflow file

In the file picker, open the Session-6 folder and then the Workflows folder.

Part 4 · Import the ready-made workflowStep 19 of 34

Select the JSON and open it

Pick the AI Recruitment Screening .json file. The preview on the right confirms it is an n8n workflow. Click Open.

Part 4 · Import the ready-made workflowStep 20 of 34

Skip the AI-tool prompt

n8n asks “Importing this from an AI tool?” You do not need the MCP connector for today: click Skip.

Part 5 · Connect GmailStep 21 of 34

Open the Gmail Trigger

Double-click the first node. It checks Gmail every minute for unread messages that match has:attachment, which is how CVs arrive. The Gmail credential is still empty, so open the Credential dropdown.

Part 5 · Connect GmailStep 22 of 34

Create the Gmail credential

Keep Managed OAuth2 (recommended) and click Sign in with Google.

Part 5 · Connect GmailStep 23 of 34

Choose the Google account

A Google pop-up opens. Select the account whose inbox will receive the job applications.

Part 5 · Connect GmailStep 24 of 34

Grant access

Read the consent screen. Tick the ongoing-access box if you want n8n to stay connected, then click Continue.

Part 5 · Connect GmailStep 25 of 34

Account connected

A green “Account connected” banner confirms the link. Close the window. Every Gmail node in this workflow can now reuse the credential.

Part 6 · Configure the AI and job settingsStep 26 of 34

Look inside Classify Email

This HTTP Request node sends each email to the Mistral chat API (POST to api.mistral.ai). Its JSON body holds a system prompt telling the model to reply only with a JSON verdict. The credential is not connected yet.

Part 6 · Configure the AI and job settingsStep 27 of 34

Set the role in Job Config

This Set node holds two values the rest of the workflow reads: job_description (text) and threshold (a number, 70 here). Change them to reuse the workflow for any role.

Part 6 · Configure the AI and job settingsStep 28 of 34

Edit the job description

Click the expand icon on job_description to open Edit Value. Paste the full job description here: responsibilities, required skills and qualifications.

Part 6 · Configure the AI and job settingsStep 29 of 34

Connect the Classify Email credential

Back in Classify Email, click Connect to Mistral Cloud under the Mistral Cloud API credential.

Part 6 · Configure the AI and job settingsStep 30 of 34

Add your Mistral API key

Paste the API key you created in the Mistral console into API Key and click Save. Treat the key like a password and never share it or put it on a slide.

Part 7 · Test and fixStep 31 of 34

Download Resume

This Gmail node uses Resource: Message, Operation: Get. The Message ID comes from the trigger and Download Attachments is on. On the left, the AI check has returned is_job_application: true.

Part 7 · Test and fixStep 32 of 34

Reuse the Gmail credential

Each Gmail node needs a credential. Select the account you already connected and the same green “Account connected” banner appears.

Part 7 · Test and fixStep 33 of 34

Fix: Meets Threshold type error

Error: “'70' is a string but was expecting a number.” Either switch on Convert types where required, or turn the value into a number (for example parseInt or .toNumber()). The candidate’s score of 95 is then compared with 70 correctly.

Part 7 · Test and fixStep 34 of 34

Store Candidate in Google Sheets

Sign in with Google, then choose the document (Candidates_data), the sheet (Sheet1) and Append Row. Map each column from the fields on the left. A red “undefined” means the expression does not match the real field name, so drag the field from the schema instead.

Done

What you have built

Email arrives→AI: is it a job application?→Download the CV→Score vs. job description→Score ≥ 70?→Log in Google Sheets→Invite or reject by email

You created an n8n account, imported a workflow, connected Gmail and an AI model, set the job description and pass mark, and fixed a typical type error. Change the job description and threshold to reuse it for any role.
